candidate.derivedAnswer: B: Their magnitudes are equal and their directions are the same
candidate.answerReason: Nonzero vectors are equal exactly when they have equal magnitudes and the same direction. Initial points may differ; zero vectors are equal to one another.

methods.label: Equality criterion
methods.explanation: For nonzero vectors, equality means equal magnitudes and the same direction; two zero vectors are also equal. Equality does not depend on the initial points. Vectors can still be equal after translation. Therefore choose B.
methods.levelReason: Uses the defining equality criterion and elementary translation, with the zero-vector case stated explicitly.
